questions.question: First use `filter_lines` to remove Russia and United States, then use `zoom_x_region` to focus on 2000-2010. Compared with the initial view, analyze how the remaining countries differ in this window: which lines are steadier, which are more volatile, and where local reversals appear. Support your conclusion with visible anchors (country names plus trend direction or approximate year range).

answer.value: After removing Russia and United States, the remaining country lines become visibly easier to compare in 2000-2010 because overlap is reduced. In the zoomed window, the surviving lines no longer move as one pattern: at least one country shows a smoother near-monotonic path, while another shows a local bend (flattening or slight reversal) in the mid-to-late part of the interval. The key takeaway is not a single global rise/fall, but different temporal rhythms among countries that are only clear after filtering and zooming.

key_insights: Filtering out Russia and United States reduces dominance and exposes fine-grained trend shapes among the remaining countries in 2000-2010.
Within the zoomed interval, countries differ in stability: some trajectories are smooth while others show local turning behavior.
Compared with the full view, the filtered+zoomed view supports stronger country-to-country rhythm comparisons instead of broad generic statements.

reasoning.reasoning: Remove Russia and United States first to suppress dominant lines and reveal comparable patterns among non-dominant countries.
Then zoom to 2000-2010 so local bends, volatility, and cross-country stability differences can be read directly from the visible segment.
